question: OpenHOI3 expeditionary forces: CExpeditionaryForceDialog, the diplomacy rows, the flow, and what a lent unit is afterwards.

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::CExpeditionaryForceDialog
addresses.signature: CExpeditionaryForceDialog* __stdcall CExpeditionaryForceDialog::CExpeditionaryForceDialog(CInGameIdler* host@ECX, CExpeditionaryForceDialog* this@stack:4, CSendExpeditionaryForceAction* action@stack:8, CDiplomacyView* view@stack:12) @EAX
addresses.comment: **The window an expedition is sent or withdrawn from** (`ExpeditionDialog`, interface/diplomacydialog.gui). 0x375BE0 to the `ret 0xC` at 0x376176; the one caller is DiplomacyView_OpenActionDialog at 0x38BD75 for token 0x71A. CEU3Dialog's constructor with `ExpeditionDialog`, then its own vftable; +0xEC kind = 2 (land), +0xF0 the host, +0xF4 a clone of the action (slot 16), +0xF8 the view, and three empty selection lists (+0xFC land, +0x10C air, +0x11C navy). `LeftShield` the action's actor (+8/+0xC), `RightShield` its recipient (+0x10/+0x14); Title = the action's slot 10 GetTitle (`SENDEXPED`/`RETRIEVEEXPED`/`RESENDEXPED`, each + `TITLE`). `ArmyButton`, `AirButton`, `NavyButton` get glue to OnArmyButton (kind 2), OnAirButton (0), OnNavyButton (1); AgreeButton's text is `ACCEPT`, DeclineButton's `DECLINE`. RebuildUnitList, then the description; finally `diplo_popup_chance_bg` and `chance_string` are hidden (no chance text is ever written - the AI's answer is shown nowhere in this window). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-expedition.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Read whole in decompilation (expdec_dlg.log) and against the listing at 0x775C45/0x776176; ret 0xC checked. Its single caller 0x78BD75 in DiplomacyView_OpenActionDialog. The kind default and the three lists are the constructor's stores; wrong if RTTI gave a different class to the vftable at 0x15DA284.

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 1, every frame. Which country's units the list shows: value (+0x24) set (send) the player's; value clear, ClaimType (+0x28) 1 (RESEND) the player's filtered on the recipient (+0x10), ClaimType 0 (RETRIEVE) the recipient's filtered on the actor (+8). CountUnitRows gives the rows the list should have: **the same number as it holds -> each row's slot 8 Update, a different number -> RebuildUnitList.** `AgreeButton` is disabled (state 3 -> slot 0xB8/0xBC) unless one of the three selection lists has an entry. Ends with CEU3Dialog::Update.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the row-count comparison is at 0x777890-0x7778BA of the decompilation lines 439-478 of expdec_dlg.log. Wrong if the count compared were not the list box's size at +8 of its entry list.

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::Accept
addresses.comment: Slot 5, `AgreeButton`. The action's date = tick; MakeCommand (action slot 6) posted through the host (slot 18 -> +0x38 slot 6); CDiplomacyView::EnableActionListUnlessAutomated; the dialog marked closed (+0x64 = 1). So whatever row was picked goes as the action's unit (+0x2C, set in ExpeditionDialog_SelectRow), and with nothing picked Agree cannot be pressed.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the slot-5 binding of AgreeButton is the one CDiplomacyDialog::Accept already records for every dialog (CEU3Dialog's constructor).

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::Decline
addresses.comment: Slot 6, `DeclineButton`: nothing is posted. Where the view's selected country is still the recipient, CDiplomacyView::RebuildActionList(view, recipient); the dialog marked closed. (No influence, no message: the cost is charged only by Apply on the posted PROPOSE.)

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::IsStillOpen
addresses.comment: Slot 7: open while the view's slot 7 (Visible, inferred) answers true and the view's current dialog (+0x518) is empty or this one.

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::RebuildUnitList
addresses.comment: Empties `unitlist_list`, FillUnitRows for this kind and country (see Update), and re-selects every row whose unit is in one of the three selection lists (ExpeditionDialog_SelectRow), keeping the list's scroll position proportionally. So a change of the unit tree or of the kind buttons keeps what was ticked. Also the land/air/navy buttons' tail.

addresses.name: ExpeditionDialog_UpdateDescription
addresses.comment: `Description`. Builds the selected unit's half first, the first non-empty of the three lists: land `EXPEDNEWDESC_ARMY`, navy `EXPEDNEWDESC_NAVY`, air `EXPEDNEWDESC_AIR`, each $UNIT$ (unit slot 7), $NUM$ (ExpeditionDialog_CountDescendants, which counts the unit itself and everything under it - so it is 1 for a lone unit and the units of the subtree, not divisions or brigades; the air case starts it at 1), $PROV$ (the province's slot 7). Then the head: value set -> `SENDEXPEDNEWDESC` with $RECIPIENT$ (the action's recipient); value clear -> `RETRIEVEEXPEDNEWDESC` with $RECIPIENT$ = the recipient when ClaimType is 1, the actor when 0, and $DATE$ = tick + (defines.diplomacy +0xB0 EXPEDITION_RETURN_TIME when ClaimType 1, +0xB4 EXPEDITION_RECLAIM_TIME when 0)/1000 x 24 hours, written by the hour form of the date (FUN_0044CB60, `%d %s %d %d:00`). Head + unit's half = the text. Bare `ret 4` argument: the dialog.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole (expdec_dlg2.log). Wrong if the +0xB0/+0xB4 read at 0x77692x-0x7769xx were swapped; it is read against the defines record, which names both.

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::CountUnitRows
addresses.signature: int __thiscall CExpeditionaryForceDialog::CountUnitRows(CExpeditionaryForceDialog* this, CUnitList* units, int depth, bool returning, CCountryTag* owner)
addresses.comment: What FillUnitRows would add, for Update's rebuild test. Same filter (see FillUnitRows). `ret 0x10`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole; the filter is identical to 0x777630's.

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::FillUnitRows
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CExpeditionaryForceDialog::FillUnitRows(CExpeditionaryForceDialog* this, void* list, CUnitList* units, int depth, int kind, bool returning, CCountryTag* owner)
addresses.comment: Fills `unitlist_list` in the list's own order (no sort), one CBrowserItem per unit (operator new 0xE8), and recursively its children straight after it **only for land units and only while the unit's outliner_expanded (+0xB4) is set**. A unit is skipped unless: (send, `returning` false) it has no expeditionary owner; (withdraw, `returning` true) its expeditionary owner id is the owner's **and** its expeditionary_date (+0x294) is at least defines.end_date (so a unit already told to go home is not listed), and at depth 0 not if its parent is an expeditionary unit of the same owner. Then by `kind`: 2 land (slot 15), 0 air (slot 17), 1 navy (slot 16). `ret 0x18`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole. The send-mode branch also skips units with a parent at depth 0 for land; that test is at piVar1[0x78]... lines 976-979.

addresses.name: ExpeditionDialog_SelectRow
addresses.comment: A row's box ticked. Clears all three selection lists and unticks every other row; adds the row's unit (a by-value CRef in a 0x34-byte node) to the list of the current kind; ticks the visible rows of its children (ExpeditionDialog_CountExpandedDescendants, CBrowserItem_SetTicked); stores the row's CRef as the action's unit (+0x2C); ExpeditionDialog_UpdateDescription. So only one unit is ever chosen. `ret 8`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole (expdec_dlg2.log). The row's slot 4 and RebuildUnitList call it.

addresses.name: ExpeditionDialog_DeselectRow
addresses.comment: A row's box unticked. **For kind 2 (land) and 0 (air) only**, the node for the row's unit is taken out of that kind's list and every child's with ExpeditionDialog_DeselectDescendants; a fleet's is left in its list (the navy kind has no branch here - an oddity, the list's count stays and Agree stays pressable while the action's unit is emptied below). The rows of its children are unticked; the action's unit is set to the null ref; ExpeditionDialog_UpdateDescription. `ret 8`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole; the kind test is at the top, `if (+0xEC != 0) goto ...` after the kind-2 arm.

addresses.name: ExpeditionDialog_DeselectDescendants
addresses.comment: Removes each child of `unit`, recursively, from a selection list by CRef compare (node +4/+8).

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::OnAirButton
addresses.comment: `AirButton`: kind (+0xEC) = 0, then RebuildUnitList (tail jump).
addresses.evidence: Disassembled, two instructions; the glue's method pointer assignment is in the constructor.

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::OnArmyButton
addresses.comment: `ArmyButton`: kind (+0xEC) = 2, then RebuildUnitList.

addresses.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog::OnNavyButton
addresses.comment: `NavyButton`: kind (+0xEC) = 1, then RebuildUnitList.

addresses.name: ExpeditionDialog_CountExpandedDescendants
addresses.comment: The number of rows below an expanded unit: 0 when it is not outliner_expanded (+0xB4), else 1 per descendant row (each child and, recursively, its expanded descendants). Bare `ret`.

addresses.name: ExpeditionDialog_CountDescendants
addresses.comment: count + how many units are under `unit`, at every depth. Bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CBrowserItem::CBrowserItem
addresses.signature: CBrowserItem* __stdcall CBrowserItem::CBrowserItem(CBrowserItem* this, void* inGameScreen, void* owner, CUnit* unit, int depth)
addresses.comment: **The row of the expeditionary-force dialog's unit tree** (window `expedition_entry`, `unitlist_list` of interface/diplomacydialog.gui; 0xE8 bytes). `ret 0x14`. Holds the unit by CRef (+0xB0..), the in-game screen (+0xD8), its depth (+0xDC) and the dialog (+0xE0). `expand` -> CBrowserItem_OnExpand, `select_frame` is a checkbox (ticked -> slot 4 OnSelect through thunk 0x67A310; unticked -> CBrowserItem_OnUnticked). **`select_frame` is disabled for a theatre** (oob_level +0x1F4 == 0): a theatre is listed and cannot be chosen. `name` = the unit's slot 7, `location` = its province's name; `counter_type` the sprite GFX_counter_ + the first brigade's type (only where intel_level is 3 or more and it has a brigade); `counter_size` frame 6/5/4/3 for levels 0/1/2/3, 2 for a division with more than one brigade else 1, 2 for level 5 (`+1` of the oob_level switch) and 1 otherwise. Then its slot 8 Update. One caller, the recursive CExpeditionaryForceDialog::FillUnitRows. CUnitBrowserEntry does not derive from it: both derive from CStandardlistboxItem directly. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-expedition.md, section 1.3.
addresses.revises: Was inferred, outline only ('the row of the dialog's unit tree', 'only the outline was read'); now read whole.

addresses.name: CBrowserItem::OnSelect
addresses.comment: Slot 4: the checkbox ticked. Resolves the unit (nothing if gone) and calls ExpeditionDialog_SelectRow(dialog +0xE0, this).

addresses.name: CBrowserItem::Update
addresses.comment: Slot 8, every frame through CExpeditionaryForceDialog::Update. Nothing where the unit is gone or is not a land unit. `expand` disabled where children_count (+0x1EC) is 0, enabled where it is not. The row's window is moved to x = depth x `browser_offset`.x, y kept (`browser_offset` is sidebar.gui's, x 10) - the same placing as CUnitBrowserEntry's.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and the tail read on the listing (imul at 0x77566F).

addresses.name: CBrowserItem_OnExpand
addresses.comment: `expand` pressed: flips the unit's outliner_expanded (+0xB4) - the same flag the outliner uses; the row list is rebuilt only by the next frame's Update seeing a different row count.

addresses.name: CBrowserItem_OnUnticked
addresses.comment: `select_frame` unticked: ExpeditionDialog_DeselectRow(dialog, this); the box's own state is then forced unticked (it keeps its look through the base glue otherwise); a theatre's box is disabled again.

addresses.name: CBrowserItem_SetTicked
addresses.comment: Ticks `select_frame`'s state and frame; disables it for a theatre.

addresses.name: CBrowserItem_SetUnticked
addresses.comment: Unticks `select_frame`, leaving a disabled one alone; disables it for a theatre.

addresses.name: CBrowserItem_CopyUnitRef
addresses.comment: Copies the row's CRef (+0xB0.. +0xBC name) into `out`. Bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CAskExpedition_CountDescendants
addresses.comment: **The $NUM$ of ASKEXPEDITIONREQDESC, and it is wrong in the original.** `e = count; for each child: e = e + 1; e = e + f(child, e)`; returns e. So it is 0 for a unit with no children (the popup offers '0 Divisions'), 2 for one childless child, and grows much faster than the unit's children past that - each child's recursion adds its accumulated count to the running total. Bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: Read on the listing, 0x6114C0-0x6114F0, the `add edi,eax` at 0x6114E5 after the recursive call. Wrong if the recursive call's return were discarded; it is added.

addresses.name: CAskExpedition::CAskExpedition
addresses.signature: CAskExpedition* __stdcall CAskExpedition::CAskExpedition(CInGameIdler* host@ECX, CAskExpedition* this@stack:4, CSendExpeditionaryForceAction* action@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: An expeditionary force offered: `ASKEXPEDITIONREQDESC` with $ACTOR$, $UNIT$, $NUM$, $PROV$ and $TYPE$ from EXP_SHIP/EXP_SQUADRON/EXP_DIVISION; `ACCEPT`/`DECLINE`. The $NUM$ is CAskExpedition_CountDescendants(unit, 0), 0 for a lone unit and otherwise inflated - see that entry. $TYPE$: EXP_SHIP where the unit is naval (slot 16), EXP_SQUADRON where air (slot 17), else EXP_DIVISION. Shields actor/recipient, only when the action's type is PROPOSE; Accept and Decline are CDiplomacyDialog's.
addresses.revises: Adds $NUM$'s actual computation and the arms of $TYPE$.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::IsSelectable
addresses.comment: Slot 14, read whole. actor != recipient, else false. **With `value` set (send)**: a diplomat en route to the recipient is false; influence (100000 under g_UnlimitedDiploInfluence, else diplo_influence) below EXPEDITION_INFLUENCE_COST (+0xAC) is false. **A ref that resolves to a theatre (oob_level +0x1F4 == 0) is false; a ref that resolves to anything else, or that does not resolve at all, is true.** So a fresh 'send' row, whose unit is the null ref, is NOT greyed for that reason - the dialog is what makes sure a unit is chosen. With `value` clear nothing about the diplomat or influence applies: a withdrawal row is only actor != recipient and the theatre test.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole. The old comment said an unresolved ref greys the fresh row; the code is `if (ref resolves && unit is theatre) return false; return true`.
addresses.revises: Comment corrected: an unresolved unit ref does not grey the row; only a resolved theatre does. Confidence inferred -> confirmed, read whole.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::GetDescription
addresses.comment: Slot 11, read whole. Same actor: ACT_NO_SELF. A diplomat en route and value set: ENROUTE with $DATE$ (the status's next_offer_allowed, as a string passed through sprintf as a format - see FINDINGS-agreements). Value set and influence short: DIP_NO_INFL, $INF$ the cost with 0 decimals. Value set otherwise: SENDEXPEDDESC. Value clear, in every case: RETRIEVEEXPEDDESC for ClaimType TAKE, else RESENDEXPEDDESC.
addresses.revises: Confidence inferred -> confirmed; read whole; text otherwise the same.

addresses.name: CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
**Slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB934), read end to end 2026-10-06 - 1,226 instructions, 0x6395B0 to the one bare `ret` at 0x63A853, `retsBefore` empty, 12 int3, then slot 11 at 0x63A860.** `this` in ECX and then in frame slot [esp+0x20], nothing on the stack. The earlier `inferred` reading was right about the name and about every call it listed; what follows corrects nothing and adds the order.

**It is in three parts.** (1) A message is built - `ACTOR`, `RECIPIENT`, `RECPIENT` (the engine's own typo), `MESSAGE_HEAD_CHAN`, `MESSENGER` and `UNIT` substitutions, the last of them at 0x639DD1 taking `&this->unit (+0x2C)` through `CRef_Resolve` (0x19A190) and then calling **slot 7 of the resolved `CUnit` with no null test at all** (`mov edx,[eax]` at 0x639DE8). (2) At 0x639EBB the unit ref is resolved again through `CRef_ResolveAndCache` (0x2DE10) and **this** result is tested: zero jumps to the epilogue at 0x63A83F and the action does nothing. So the guard is 0xEA bytes *after* the dereference - harmless in practice only because slot 13 `IsValid` (0x63AD90) refuses a null-unit action before `CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute` (0x60E120) ever reaches slot 7. (3) The work, keyed on the base's `type` (+0x18) and `value` (+0x24), not on `ClaimType`:

- `type == 0` PROPOSE and `value` set (0x639ED5): the influence cost, `-GetDefines()->diplomacy (+0xBC)->+0xAC` (EXPEDITION_INFLUENCE_COST), through 0xF4E50 on the actor
- `type == 2` ACCEPT and `value` set (0x639F2F): the hand-over. `0x1B9A30(unit, 1)`, then `unit->+0x294` from the defines, then - only when `unit->+0x290` is still zero - `unit->+0x28C`/`+0x290` saved from the other country's `+0x124`/`+0x128`, which is how the brigade finds its way home; then 0xE0860, 0xE0830 and 0xE06F0 move it between the two countries' unit lists, and 0x1D3840 runs when `unit->+0x1EC` is set
- `value` clear, **whatever the type** (0x63A519; the withdrawal rows are type 3): the unit's expeditionary_date (+0x294) = tick + EXPEDITION_RETURN_TIME/1000 x 24 hours - no message, no hand-over; the host's daily pass (RunCountryDailyPass, 0x4DB1AD..0x4DB418) sends it home once the date is past, the first expired unit of the host's list per day. EXPEDITION_RECLAIM_TIME (+0xB4) is never read here, though the dialog's text uses it for a RETRIEVE.
- `type == 1` DECLINE and `value` set: only the news. `OUREXPDEC` and the `diplomaticfailure` sound to the actor's player; **no refund of the influence, charged at PROPOSE**.
- In the accept branch the news is `OUREXPACC` (success sound) to the actor's player and **`EXPOTHER` to every other player, the recipient's included**.

**`ClaimType` (+0x28) is never read in the whole body** - a grep of all 1,226 instructions for a `[reg + 0x28]` operand on any base but ESP returns nothing, while the same grep finds `[reg + 0x18]` and `[reg + 0x24]` at fourteen sites. So the direction of an expedition is carried by `value`, and TAKE/SEND only choose a localisation key in slot 20. EXPEDITION_RETURN_TIME (+0xB0) is read and EXPEDITION_RECLAIM_TIME (+0xB4) is not, as the earlier entry said; the news keys are `OUREXPACC`, `OUREXPDEC` and `EXPOTHER`, with `diplomaticsuccess`/`diplomaticfailure` as the sound.
addresses.evidence: The branch at 0xA39F1C: `cmp [esi+0x18],2; jne 0xa3a510; cmp [esi+0x24],bl; je 0xa3a519`; 0xA3A510 `cmp [esi+0x24],bl; jne 0xa3a606`; 0xA3A519 is the date block, reached for value clear at any type. Read from the listing and the decompilation; OUREXPDEC is in the value-set branch of the news tail at LAB_a3a60a. Wrong if 0xA3A519 were reached only for type 2.
addresses.revises: Comment said value-clear ACCEPT at 0x63A519 is 'the return leg, keyed OUREXPDEC and EXPOTHER'. It is the recall: it only sets the unit's date; those keys are the offer's news. Corrects FINDINGS-diploaction.md section 31 too.

addresses.name: CCountry_AddToLentList
addresses.comment: Appends `unit` to the country's expeditionary_units_lent (+0xBBC) unless already there. `ret 4`. Called by Apply, CSendExpeditionCommand::Execute and _TransferSubtree, CUnit_TransferChildren and CUnit::LoadKey (expeditionary_owner, on load).
addresses.evidence: Listing 0x4E0860-0x4E08C4; callers by findRefs-style reading of the sites listed.

addresses.name: CCountry_RemoveFromUnits
addresses.comment: Unlinks `unit` from the country's units (+0xBAC). Bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CCountry_AddInfluence
addresses.comment: diplo_influence (+0xA88) += amount, held at 0 and above. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CUnit_TransferChildren
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnit_TransferChildren(void* ignored@ECX, CUnit* parent@stack:4, CCountryTag* target@stack:8, bool detachOnly@stack:12)
addresses.comment: Each child of `parent` (a copy of the children list is walked): CUnit_LeaveParent(child, 1), and with detachOnly set nothing more - so CUnit::ReturnFromExpedition's call, with 1, leaves the children detached on the host's list. With detachOnly 0 (CSendExpeditionaryForceAction::Apply's hand-over): where the child has no expeditionary owner it gets its owner's and goes on that country's lent list (CCountry_AddToLentList); it leaves its owner's Units, CCountry::AddUnit(target), CUnit_AttachToParent under `parent`, and recursion where it has children of its own. **Unlike CSendExpeditionCommand_TransferSubtree it does not touch expeditionary_date** (a new unit's date is defines.end_date by the constructor, so a child is not sent home by the daily pass). ECX is only passed on to the recursion. `ret 0xC`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled whole (expdec_mech.log), and the census of +0x294 writers: CUnit::CUnit, CSendExpeditionCommand::Execute and _TransferSubtree, Apply twice, and no others.

addresses.name: CUnit_PictureCultureName
addresses.no_signature: __fastcall with the unit in EDX and ECX unused; only the body was read, and the argument is typed by this fragment's reading alone.
addresses.comment: The name of the graphical culture the unit's counter (RebuildAvatar's lookups) is drawn in: from the first brigade's builder (+0x38, else its owner +0x98), overridden by the expeditionary owner (+0x290) when the unit has one - a lent division wears its lender's sprites. Unnamed by the record's readers until now; the name is ours; only this reading of the fragment.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 12 lines. Whether every caller is RebuildAvatar was not settled.

structs.name: CExpeditionaryForceDialog
structs.evidence: RTTI: CEU3Dialog at offset 0 in hoi3_tfh-classes.json; 0x15DA284 is the vftable the constructor writes.

structs.name: CBrowserItem
structs.comment: A row of the expedition dialog's unit tree.
structs.evidence: RTTI as above; 0x15DA1F0 written by the constructor.

struct_fields.name: kind
struct_fields.comment: Which units the list shows: 2 land (default), 0 air, 1 navy. Set by the three kind buttons.

struct_fields.name: host
struct_fields.comment: The in-game screen; Accept posts through its slot 18.

struct_fields.name: action
struct_fields.comment: The dialog's clone of the action; its unit (+0x2C) is what a tick stores.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor; SelectRow and DeselectRow store +0x2C through it.

struct_fields.name: view
struct_fields.comment: The diplomacy view the dialog came from.

struct_fields.name: selected_land
struct_fields.comment: Head of the land kind's selection list (nodes of 0x34 bytes with a CRef by value); tail +0x100, count +0x104, no-unlink byte +0x108. The air kind's is the same at +0x10C/+0x110/+0x114 and the navy kind's at +0x11C/+0x120/+0x124. Only one list is non-empty: a tick clears all three first.

struct_fields.name: unit
struct_fields.comment: The row's unit, by value: pointer at +0xB0, the persistent pair at +0xB4/+0xB8.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor's FUN_0042DD70 call; the slot bodies resolve it.

struct_fields.name: depth
struct_fields.comment: The row's depth in the unit tree (0 top); its indent is depth x browser_offset.x.

struct_fields.name: dialog
struct_fields.comment: The dialog the row belongs to.

struct_fields.name: expeditionary_date
struct_fields.comment: **When an expeditionary unit goes home, in ticks; defines.end_date (the constructor's default and Apply's on the hand-over) means no recall pending.** A withdrawal (Apply, value clear) sets it to tick + EXPEDITION_RETURN_TIME x 24; the host's daily pass (RunCountryDailyPass 0x4DB1AD..0x4DB418) sends home the first of its units past it each day; the dialog's rows and the withdrawal rows of GetDiplomaticActionsToward test >= defines.end_date; only the save (expeditionary_date, written with expeditionary_owner where set) and the two tooltip routines read it else. Read only as a CUnit field: the census of +0x294 finds other classes' same offsets.
struct_fields.evidence: Writers CUnit::CUnit (default end_date, 0x5B52B2), CSendExpeditionCommand::Execute, _TransferSubtree, Apply twice; readers the list above. A write through a register other than a CUnit* would be missed.

slots_noted: CExpeditionaryForceDialog slot 3 is the folded EmptyTooltip and slot 4 the folded ReturnTrue; slot 0 (scalar deleting destructor) and 8-16 are CEU3Dialog's or are not this class's own, so no record.
